rivals.design:
CONSTRUCTION 1: STAGE-SPECIALISED SMT PAIRS ("walk affinity"). Repo lmmx/mibz2 at master bab0d603; the decoder src is identical to d1fd4405. Design only: nothing committed, no cargo run, no timings.

1. THE RULE. On each physical core, pin two threads to its two SMT siblings:
- the walker, on the lower CPU id;
- the compute thread, on the higher one.
Only the walker ever walks. Every other stage is shared and work-conserving within the core: MTF+RLE2, build, RLE1+CRC, and segment assembly (assembly stays on the walker because it reads the walker's SegScratch). So a core never runs two walks at once, and neither sibling idles while non-walk work is queued.

INFERRED from the cost model (sim.py variants2/out0) on three design choices:
- Giving builds only to the walker loses: +13% to +16% core time on the 8370C, and gains only -3% to -8% on AMD, against -5% to -19% for shared builds.
- Letting the walker pull jobs is no better.
- OUT=0 (the walker always finishes) costs up to +1.9% on the 8370C.

2. QUEUES (one Mutex<Queues> + one Condvar per core, two threads only; parked waits, never spins).
- mtfd: Option<Mtfd{h, ll, counts}>, a last column waiting for its build.
- built: Option<Built{h, ll, tt}>, a T-vector waiting for the walk. TT=2 T-vectors a core: one being walked, one being built or queued.
- walked: Option<Walked{h, text}>, the walk's output waiting for RLE1+CRC (OUT=1).
- free_tt (at most 2), lls (reused last-column buffers), ended.
Here h = Head{place, bit, orig_ptr, crc}. The walk writes over ll, as in Segmented::invert_in_place (src/bwt.rs:114-118). ll travels with its block, and tt goes back to free_tt as soon as the walk ends. The walk needs &mut TVector because it sets START bits and clears them again (bwt.rs:908-910, 1192-1194); build rewrites every entry, so reusing a tt is safe.

Compute loop, in priority order:
(a) Build, if mtfd is waiting, built is empty and a tt is free.
(b) Else MTF, if mtfd is empty: lock the shared jobs queue and recv, as worker does today (parallel.rs:418-426). Recycle the symbols right after MTF, not after the whole decode.
(c) Else finish a walked block.
(d) Else wait on the core's cv.

Walker loop, in priority order:
(a) Walk built.
(b) Else, if mtfd is waiting and a tt is free, build it here and walk it at once.
(c) Else finish walked.
(d) Else, if ended and everything is empty, exit; otherwise wait.
After a walk: if walked is free, push the result there for whichever thread is idle; otherwise finish it itself.

Deadlock audit (INFERRED):
- The compute thread waits only when mtfd is full, no tt is free and walked is empty. Every tt is then being built, queued or walked, so the walker has work.
- Only the compute thread needs the scanner, and it recvs only when mtfd is empty. The walker can do B, W and F alone, so a core always drains.

3. ORDERING. Unchanged: publish() inserts into State.ready by place, and the reader takes blocks in order (parallel.rs:231-280), so errors still come in order.
- In flight per core: at most 6 (in MTF, mtfd, two T-vector holders, walked, the walker finishing), so at most 12 at 4t. That is within the 4 x threads = 16 window (SLOTS_PER_THREAD=4, parallel.rs:37; lib.rs:375).
- Cross-core balance comes from pulling: a core takes a job only when its mtfd is empty.
- A slow core holding the oldest block fills the window, and the scanner then waits. This is self-limiting, as today.

4. BALANCE PER CPU MODEL. Alone c/B, OBSERVED from phases rows (runs 42011789918 for the 7763, 42020095581 for the 9V74, 42008210159 for the 8370C). Walk W includes assembly; non-walk N = scanner + MTF + build + RLE1 + CRC.
- 7763: W 4.33 vs N 5.91 (walk 42% alone). Co-run under C: 9.18 vs 8.26, walker-bound by 11%, so the compute thread idles about 5% (sim).
- 9V74: 4.22 vs 5.42. Co-run 9.37 vs 7.86, walker-bound by 19%; compute idles about 8%.
- 8370C: 7.27 vs 6.18. Co-run 10.6 vs 11.2, compute-bound by 5%; the walker absorbs about 0.3 c/B of builds and finishes a block.
- 8573C: no per-stage factors measured; the walk is 40-53% of 4t wall.

Under M or P the walk's co-run cost falls, so every model turns compute-bound and the walker builds whenever no T-vector is queued (all INFERRED). No per-model constant is needed: work conservation sets the split.

Overflow walking (the compute thread walks when it would otherwise idle): +0.1% to +1.9% under P, about 0 under C. Left out.

The scanner and reader stay unpinned (the process mask) and fill idle vCPUs. Restricting the scanner to the walker CPUs is a prototype arm only.

5. WHEN IT ENGAGES. Plan::for_threads gives Plan::Staged{pairs: cores} only when all of these hold:
- the topology is readable (Linux);
- fewer than COOP_MIN_CORES=6 cores are used (teams first, unchanged; parallel.rs:494, 540-555);
- threads == 2 x allowed cores;
- every allowed core has exactly 2 allowed CPUs, each id below 1024.

Every other case is Plan::Workers(threads), today's pool:
- no SMT, SMT off, or one CPU a core allowed (the bench's 2t on CPUs 0,2);
- 1t;
- odd or partial counts, such as 3t on CI (a v2 could add 1 pair plus 1 lone worker on its own core);
- oversubscription (8t on 4 vCPUs);
- SMT-4.

The i9 (10 cores, 20 CPUs) never engages with its full mask. At up to 5 threads the workers sit on separate cores; at 6 or more, teams. Its binding term is L3 capacity (FULL_TABLE cap, parallel.rs:548-553), not siblings. Staged engages there only if the affinity mask is cut to 5 or fewer whole cores and threads = 2 x cores. Staged plus teams on the i9 would be a separate construction.

wikidata-pq's split never engages it either: its default is one thread a physical core, at most 4 (wikidata-pq src/wikidata/dump.py:165-169). So the end-to-end release ETA is unchanged unless that policy is revisited.

6. FALLBACK.
- Plan::Workers(n) is the explicit escape hatch (StreamDecoder::planned, BzReader::parallel_planned, the ab.rs arm mibz2-workers at examples/ab.rs:446-461).
- At construction each staged thread saves its mask (sched_getaffinity), pins itself (sched_setaffinity(0, 128, mask)), reports to a Start{Mutex, Condvar} handshake and blocks on the decision. Precedent for extern "C" sched_setaffinity without the libc crate: examples/ab.rs:105-108. The crate stays std-only.
- The constructor decides Staged only if every pin succeeded. Otherwise each thread restores its mask and runs today's worker::<Segmented>(&shared, &jobs, k) unchanged.
- The scanner is spawned after the decision and is identical in both modes, with the same mpsc job channel.
- Planned re-reads the topology for Staged; if it no longer fits, it builds Workers(2 x pairs).

7. MEMORY. INFERRED from buffer sizes: tt is 3.6 MB; ll 0.9 MB; SegScratch about 1.8 MB reserved (cap = 2n/ns + 64 x 512 segments, bwt.rs:911-916).
- Today at 4t: 4 tt (14.4 MB) + 4 ll (3.6) + 4 SegScratch (about 7.3) ≈ 25 MB of worker scratch.
- Staged with TT=2: 4 tt (14.4) + at most 10 ll (9.0) + 2 SegScratch (3.7) ≈ 27 MB at the cap.
- Symbols are freed after MTF, earlier than today (up to 1.8 MB each).
- Net: about +2 MB at most, against an OBSERVED 4t RSS of 74-78 MB (1t 25 MB; accounting FALSIFIER, bench 41980640481). That is about +3%.
- TT=3 adds +7.2 MB and gains nothing in the model (variants.py: TT2 = TT3 within 0.2%).
- Blocks in flight are still bounded by the window.

8. CODE SHAPE.

src/lib.rs: split decode_block (lib.rs:314-362) into stage functions, so both paths run the same code (byte-identical output; room_segments is #[inline(never)], bwt.rs:886):
- pub(crate) fn mtf_stage(b, k, ll, counts) -> Result<(), ErrorKind>: mtf plus the orig_ptr check;
- pub(crate) fn finish_stage(text, stored_crc, k, out) -> Result<u32, ErrorKind>: unrle plus crc32 plus the compare.
decode_block calls them.

src/parallel.rs:
(1) Topology. fn allowed_cores() -> Option<Vec<Vec<usize>>> returns the allowed CPUs grouped by (package, core_id), each group sorted, ordered by first CPU. It replaces physical_cores()'s set, and physical_cores() becomes allowed_cores().map(|c| c.len()).
(2) Plan. Add the variant Staged { pairs: usize }. workers() and threads() give 2 x pairs; window() gives slots. Change the signature to plan_with(threads, cores: Option<&[Vec<usize>]>, l3) with the rule in section 5.
(3) Pinning. A #[cfg(target_os="linux")] mod pin with get() / set(&Mask) / only(cpu), where Mask is [u64; 16].
(4) Types. struct Start; struct Core { q: Mutex<Queues>, cv: Condvar }; struct Queues as in section 2; Head, Mtfd, Built, Walked.
(5) Constructor. fn staged(cpus: Vec<[usize; 2]>, slots, k) -> StreamDecoder: Shared, channels and the jobs Arc<Mutex<Receiver>> as with_inverse does.
- Spawn thread names that keep today's form: mibz2-{2c} is the walker and mibz2-{2c+1} the compute thread. bench/report.py:318 counts workers by mibz2-\d+, and examples/occupancy.rs:245-246 assigns roles by name.
- Then Start::decide, then the scanner, unchanged.
(6) fn compute(shared, core, jobs, k) and fn walker(shared, core, k), as in section 2:
- Each stage runs under catch_unwind.
- On a panic in build or walk: drop that tt (TVector::default()), reset the walker's SegScratch, and publish ErrorKind::Internal for that place. Buffer counts are kept on every path, so no tt is lost and no wait is stranded.
- Cancellation: check cancelled before each stage, and recycle without working. Compute keeps draining the jobs channel, as worker does at :438-439.
- End: when recv returns Err, compute sets ended and notifies; the walker drains, then exits.
(7) fn publish(shared, h, res, syms/out recycling): worker's tail at :462-471, factored out.
(8) Trace marks. JobLock/JobRecv/JobGot/DecodeStart on compute; Ready at publish. Occupancy's per-block CPU (one thread a block) needs new stage marks later; the bench does not.
(9) Size: about 300-400 lines plus tests.

9. TESTS.
- plan_with on synthetic topologies:
  - [[0,1],[2,3]]: 4 gives Staged{2}; 2, 3 and 8 give Workers;
  - [[0],[2]] with 2 gives Workers;
  - [[0,1]] with 2 gives Staged{1};
  - SMT-4 gives Workers;
  - the i9 assertions unchanged.
- The whole parallel test suite (errors in order, bad CRC or orig_ptr or runs at every position, cancel, drop mid-stream, panic to Internal, short blocks, multi-stream, slots = threads) run under Plan::Staged through a cfg(test) no-pin switch, so the queues run on any CI box.
- A fallback test: pinning to an impossible CPU must fall back to the pool and still decode.
rivals.cost_model:
MODEL (INFERRED). Scripts in c1-stagespec/: sim.py; results in final.txt, grid.txt, out1.txt; xkernel.py.

Set-up:
- One core, two siblings, in continuous time.
- Stage X progresses at rate 1/f(X|Y), where Y is the sibling's current stage. An idle sibling gives f = 1.
- Pair factors are f(X|Y) = 1 + a_X g(X,Y). g is the outcome's pattern. Each a_X is fitted so that 'today' (two independent full chains a core, S M B W F, ±20% per-stage jitter) reproduces the OBSERVED four-copy mixed factor of every stage.

Inputs (OBSERVED, census/falsify-walk-smt/factors.py over the three phases runs):
- 7763: S 1.43, M 1.33, B 1.43, W 2.12, F 1.48.
- 9V74: S 1.32, M 1.23, B 1.76, W 2.22, F 1.56.
- 8370C: S 1.56, M 1.54, B 2.25, W 1.46, F 1.94.
Alone c/B as in the design section.

Staged arm: walker and compute threads with TT=2, LL=2, OUT=1, work-conserving except that only the walker walks.

Sanity check: under C with compute independent of its sibling, staged is -1.0% to +0.4%. Re-pairing cannot gain when the sibling's type does not matter, as it should not.

CLOSED FORM, the balanced approximation (INFERRED). It matches the sim within about 1 point where the calibration converged.
- Today's core time a block: T0 = (W F_W + N F_N) / 2.
- Gain G ≈ -[ s_W (1 - f_W|N / F_W) + s_N (1 - f_N|W / F_N) ].
- s_W is the four-copy walk share (OBSERVED): 0.527 (7763), 0.543 (9V74), 0.488 (8370C). F_W and F_N are the mixed factors.
- f_W|N is the walk beside the compute thread's real mix: f_W|N = Σ_k w_k f_W|k, with w_k the compute stages' co-run time shares (7763: MTF about 0.32, build 0.37, scanner 0.21, finish 0.10).
- Because F_W = p f_W|W + (1 - p) f_W|N, the walk term equals -s_W p (f_W|W - f_W|N) / F_W, with p ≈ s_W. So a walk gain requires walk-beside-walk to exceed the mixed 2.12-2.22 on AMD. With f_W|W ≤ 2.2 on the 7763, f_W|N ≥ 2.03 and the walk term is ≤ 2.2%.
- Imbalance:
  - walker-bound (W f_W|N > N f_N|W): T = W + N f_N|W (1 - 1/f_W|N);
  - compute-bound: T = W f_W|N + (f_N|N / 2)(N - W f_W|N / f_N|W).

TO 4T WALL (INFERRED).
- The frame is OBSERVED: wall ≈ total CPU / (4u), with u4 0.953-0.973 (accounting; #181's -3.5% CPU against -3.2% wall, run 41979947814).
- Dilution: wall gain ≈ 0.93 x core gain. Worker plus scanner is about 92-94% of 4t CPU; the reader, the sampler and the fixed start and tail are not modelled.
- Overhead: +0.3% to +1.5%:
  - 2-3 same-core handoffs a block, about 2-5 µs each against about 2.3 ms of co-run CPU a block (occupancy 41976148952 b.cpu_ms 2.26), at most about 0.4%;
  - the pin handshake once, about 50 µs;
  - pinned threads unable to migrate when the scanner or reader preempts them, ±1%, unmeasured.

PRIOR FROM EXISTING DATA (INFERRED, confounded).
- The phases unused-walk passes give the sibling different walk shares p: room 0.527, flagged 0.641, bitmap 0.787 on the 7763. If pair factors were kernel-independent, F = f_W|N + p (f_W|W - f_W|N).
- 7763: slope 0.14, so f_W|N 2.05 and f_W|W 2.19; walk term -1.8%. C-like.
- 9V74: slope 0.50, so 1.95 and 2.44; walk term -6.6%. Weak P.
- 8370C: slope 2.9, which is impossible; the kernels differ intrinsically there ('the walks with the most work per byte lose the most', walk.md FALSIFIER). No Intel prior.
- Confounds: the kernels' own SMT sensitivities differ (bitmap: 12 lanes, no prefetch), and pass alignment across copies is approximate.
rivals.gain_under_C:
(C) Any busy sibling costs the walk about 2x, so f_W|N ≈ f_W|W ≈ F_W.

The walk term is about 0; only the compute side can move.

Core time, sim (final.txt), INFERRED:
- compute side flat: 7763 -0.5%, 9V74 -1.0%, 8370C +0.4%;
- compute prefers a walking sibling (f_N|W - 1 = 0.6 (f_N|N - 1)): -3.9%, -5.2%, -4.7%;
- compute dislikes it: +2.7%, +1.8%, +3.5%.

4T WALL BOUNDS (x0.93, plus +0.3% to +1.5% overhead): -4.5% to +4.8%, central about +0.3%.

The 1t and 2t rows are unchanged (staged does not engage).

Verdict: no gain. Do not build. Write a journal entry and add a line to the Rejected list.

If the matrix shows C for the walk but compute-beside-walk ≤ 0.9 x compute-beside-compute, a pure compute-side pairing is worth at most about -4% to -5%. That is not worth the pinning and the complexity.
rivals.gain_under_M:
(M) Only memory-heavy siblings cost.

Modelled pattern:
- walk beside MTF, scanner or RLE1/CRC: 1.05-1.13;
- walk beside build or walk: about 2.2-2.3 on AMD, 1.5 on Intel.

The build is treated as memory-heavy (256 store streams into 3.6 MB). Under the 'only the walk is heavy' variant, the fit needs f_W|W of 3.9-5.0 to reproduce the mixed 2.12-2.22, which is not plausible.

Core time, sim (final.txt), INFERRED:
- 7763: -18.4% (compute-side variants -14.6% to -21.3%);
- 9V74: -19.4% (-17.6% to -23.4%);
- 8370C: -9.6% (-6.5% to -15.5%).

4T WALL BOUNDS:
- AMD -12% to -21%, central about -16%;
- Intel -5% to -14%, central about -8%.

The walk still runs beside builds for about a third of its time (the compute thread's mix). Avoiding that by giving builds to the walker loses: -7% instead of -17% on the 7763, and +13% on the 8370C. So no M-specific schedule is better than the shared build.

Verdict: build. This is the largest structural lever in the census, larger than #171's -5% to -14%.
rivals.gain_under_P:
(P) Walk-beside-compute is materially cheaper than walk-beside-walk.

Modelled point: f_W|N about F_W - 0.3 on AMD (7763 1.81, 9V74 1.87) and 1.34 on the 8370C. Consistency with the mixed factor then forces f_W|W about 2.4-2.7 on AMD, that is, two walks a core about 20-25% worse than taking turns. The pair matrix's walk|walk row checks this directly.

Core time, INFERRED:
- Closed form, compute side flat: 7763 -7.7%, 9V74 -8.6%, 8370C -4.0%.
- The sim reads -9.9%, -10.7%, -5.4%. Its AMD calibration overshoots the mixed walk factor by about +0.08, so it is about 2 points optimistic.
- Compute-side variants: ±3 to ±5 points (sim: 7763 -7.3% to -13.0%; 9V74 -6.6% to -15.3%; 8370C -1.1% to -11.5%).

4T WALL BOUNDS:
- AMD -3% to -12%, central about -7%;
- Intel +1% to -10%, central about -3%.

Strong P (f_W|N about 1.55-1.6 on AMD, 1.23 on Intel): AMD about -14% (-12% to -20%), Intel about -8%.

The existing-data prior (cross-kernel slopes) sits between C and P:
- the 7763 walk term about -1.8%, which is about -1% of wall net of overhead;
- the 9V74 about -6.6%, which is about -5% net.

Verdict: build if the predicted G ≤ -5% on the runner mix the bench lands on (the 8573C, 8370C, 7763, 9V45 and 9V74).
rivals.minimal_prototype:
A two-step plan. Step A is cheap and gates step B.

STEP A: the construction-level gate, no library change.
- What: examples/pairs.rs plus a tool: pairs arm in .github/workflows/sweep.yml. It is full tier, dispatched by hand, and runs one process without per-CPU taskset, about 6-8 minutes a dispatch.
- Arms, in one process with 4 threads pinned, the same corpus (corpora/wikidata.bz2) and the same blocks:
  - 'full': each of 4 threads runs today's chain on its own blocks (scanner, MTF, build, room walk with assembly, RLE1, CRC);
  - 'staged': per core, the walker on CPU 2c and the compute thread on 2c+1, with exactly the Queues and priority rules of the design (TT=2, OUT=1). The compute thread runs the scanner as part of its jobs.
- Protocol: rounds alternate ABBA, 10 rounds. Every block's CRC is checked.
- Report: bytes/s for each arm and the ratio with a 95% interval. Dispatch until a Zen and an Intel runner are each covered.
- Pre-registered gate:
  - pass: staged/full ≥ 1.05 with its interval excluding 1.0 on an AMD or an Intel runner, and no model below 0.98;
  - fail: a journal entry and a line in the Rejected list.
- Skip step A entirely if the pair matrix gives C (|G| < 3%).

STEP B: the decoder PR.
- Code: Plan::Staged and the parallel.rs and lib.rs changes as designed.
- Plan::for_threads selects Staged only at threads == 2 x cores on SMT-2 topologies with fewer than 6 cores, which is CI's 4t.
- Measurement: the PR-tier bench (paired A/B, 3 rounds).
  - The 4t wall decides: its 95% interval must exclude 0.
  - 1t and 2t are A/A controls; the code path is unchanged and they must sit within noise.
  - The existing mibz2-workers arm gives a same-binary pool comparator.
  - Parity must pass. The RSS row is expected at about +0-5%.
- Merge per the rules: an end-to-end figure improves beyond noise and none regresses unacceptably.
- If it gains, revisit wikidata-pq's 'one thread a physical core' default, since only then does the release ETA change.
rivals.risks:
1. Pinning inside a library. Pinned threads cannot move off a CPU that another process, or a second decoder in the same process, is using.
   - Mitigated by engaging only when the caller asks for every logical CPU in its mask (threads == 2 x cores), and by the Plan::Workers escape hatch.
   - Two decoders on the same 4 CPUs would still keep walks off sibling pairs (walkers always on the lower sibling), but could not balance across processes.
   - Seccomp or cpuset changes make pinning fail; the handshake then falls back to the pool.

2. Guest topology. If a VM's reported siblings are not real siblings, the pinning is meaningless, and could even put two walkers on one physical core. CI's 0-1|2-3 is validated by the packed-vs-spread +40% test (docs/journal/2026-10-27-four-thread-ceiling.md section 4).

3. The model is not a measurement. Pair factors are fitted patterns with no PMU behind them. The AMD calibration for P and strong P overshoots by 0.08-0.19 (marked in grid.txt), so those gains lean optimistic. The cross-kernel prior is confounded by kernel differences, and on the 7763 it already points to C (walk term -1.8%).

4. The compute-side term is as large as the walk term under C (±4%) and is entirely unmeasured. The reverse rows of the pair matrix are needed.

5. Instrumentation. The occupancy tool's per-block accounting assumes one thread a block (DecodeStart/DecodeEnd), so it needs stage marks. Thread names must stay mibz2-\d+ for bench/report.py:318 and occupancy.rs:245-246.

6. Correctness surface. There are more states for errors, cancellation, panics and shutdown. A lost tt or a stranded Condvar wait would hang the decoder. This needs the full parallel test suite under Staged, a no-pin test mode, a fallback test and a stress test with tiny windows.

7. Spin waits must not be copied from coop.rs:44-46 (SPINS 2000). On SMT siblings, spinning steals the partner's issue slots.

8. Scope. No gain for wikidata-pq at its current thread policy (one a physical core). The i9 is unaffected by design. The benefit is CI's 4t row, and any caller that asks for every logical CPU on a small SMT machine (fewer than 6 cores).

9. A single walker a core cannot take up slack when the walk dominates and walk-beside-walk is cheap (an Intel-like case). Overflow walking was modelled as a fix and gives at most 0.3% under C, so it is omitted. That is a small residual risk on models not yet measured, such as the 8573C.

rivals.design:
CONSTRUCTION 2: a per-core walk token. The code is written as a patch on d1fd4405: c2-token/token-probe.patch, in a detached worktree at c2-token/wt.
- What it adds: src/pairs.rs (new, 293 lines), src/parallel.rs (+320), src/lib.rs (+2), tests/pairs.rs (new, 129).
- STATUS: the code parses (rustfmt) and is formatted. It has NOT been type-checked or tested. Another agent's timing run held the shared build lock for over 60 minutes, with 5 jobs queued behind it, so I withdrew my job rather than compile around the lock. The check to run under flock is c2-token/check.sh.

1. Where the block splits (OBSERVED)
- On CI, Plan::for_threads(4) gives Workers(4): 2 physical cores is below COOP_MIN_CORES = 6 (parallel.rs:540-547).
- Every block therefore goes through decode_block<Segmented> (lib.rs:314-362): mtf, then Segmented::invert_in_place, which is build followed by walk_segments_room over ll (bwt.rs:114-118), then unrle and crc32.
- The split: front half = mtf + build (ll and counts in, tt out). Walk = walk_segments_room (room_segments + assemble), written over ll. Tail = RLE1 + CRC.
- ll is dead between the build and the walk. So a block between stages is just {ll, counts, tt, orig_ptr, crc, place, bit}.
- The symbols are dead once MTF has read them: on average 0.7 of the 1.3 MB of symbols held are dead (occupancy 41976148952). The design returns them to free_syms right after MTF.

2. Placement (pairs::place)
- Reads Cpus_allowed_list and groups the allowed CPUs by (package, core_id), as physical_cores() already does.
- Pairs only when threads > cores. Then (threads − cores) of the cores that have 2+ allowed CPUs each take a pair. Each pair is pinned to its core's CPU mask, not to one CPU, so CFS can still move either thread within the core (for example a preempted token holder onto the sleeping sibling's idle CPU). The remaining workers get one core each, pinned to it; any beyond that run unpinned.
- On CI at 4t this gives pairs {0,1} and {2,3}.
- The bench's 2t run (--spread, CPUs 0 and 2; ab.rs:718-720) leaves one allowed CPU per core, so place() returns None and today's decoder runs exactly: a built-in null control. 1t is BzReader::new and is untouched.
- Pinning uses sched_setaffinity through extern "C", std only, as examples/ab.rs:105-107 does.
- Plan::Workers(n) now routes through StreamDecoder::with_pairs. with_inverse::<I> stays exactly today's decoder (used by ab.rs arms and tests).
- with_pairs_on(threads, slots, k, cores) is #[doc(hidden)], so tests can impose CI's 2×2 topology on this VM, which has no SMT.

3. The token: park, never spin
- One Pair per core: Mutex<PairState> plus a Condvar.
- PairState holds: walking (Option of a member), built ([usize; 2]), asleep ([Option<Want>; 2]) and tables (Vec<TVector>).
- Why park: every wait is the length of a walk. A full block's walk at 4 copies takes 2.55 ms (7763), 2.28 ms (9V74) and 2.67 ms (8370C); INFERRED from 4-copy c/B × 0.9 MB. A futex wake costs about 5-20 µs, which is 0.2-0.9% of a walk.
- Why not spin: a spinning sibling takes issue and front-end slots from the very walk the token protects. In a VM, PAUSE loops can also exit to the hypervisor.
- Every predicate is re-checked under the lock before waiting, so a release that lands between a failed try_walk and the sleep is not lost.
- API:
  - try_walk(me): returns true if the token is free (and takes it) or was already handed to `me`; decrements built[me].
  - end_walk(me, table): returns the table to the core. Hands the token straight to the sibling if it is asleep wanting to walk and has a built block (so the releaser cannot take it back first); otherwise frees it. Notifies either way.
  - Also take_table(), built(me), give_back(me, table, was_built) and sleep(me, Want { walk, table }).

4. The table pool is the memory cap
- Each core owns exactly two TVectors: 4 at 4t, the same as today's one per worker.
- A build takes one; a walk gives it back. So each core has at most one table being walked plus one built-and-waiting or being built.
- The model (DES) shows that dropping this cap changes the gain by no more than 0.4 points, but raises live tables from a mean of 3.5-3.8 (max 4) to a mean of 4.7-5.0 (max 7-8, 25-29 MB).

5. The second-block state machine (paired_worker)
- A worker holds up to 2 blocks (Held), each either MTF'd (tt is None) or Built (tt is Some).
- At each stage end it does the first of these it can:
  1. walk its oldest Built block, if try_walk succeeds;
  2. build an MTF'd block, if take_table returns one;
  3. if it holds fewer than 2 blocks, take a job and do its MTF. It waits in recv only when it holds nothing. Otherwise it uses jobs.try_lock() + try_recv(); WouldBlock means an idle worker is asleep in recv holding the lock, so there is no job for this one;
  4. sleep(Want { walk: any Built, table: any MTF'd }).
- Stage ends are: MTF end, build end, walk end, tail end.
- walk_and_finish: walks under the token inside catch_unwind (on a panic it resets the SegScratch and returns a fresh empty table); calls end_walk BEFORE the tail, so the sibling can walk sooner; then takes a free_out buffer, runs RLE1 and the CRC check, and publishes.
- Tiny blocks (below MIN_SEGMENTED) take the token too. That costs microseconds; skipping it is an option.

6. No deadlock with the ordered output and the window
- (a) The token is held only across walk_segments_room, which takes no lock and waits on nothing. It is returned on a panic too.
- (b) A worker that holds a block never blocks on the job queue.
- (c) A worker sleeps only when it holds a Built block and the token is taken, or holds an MTF'd block and both tables are taken. A table is only ever held by a Built block or a walk. So a sleeper's sibling is either walking, or holds a Built block with the token free; in the second case the sibling's own predicate is true, so it walks rather than sleeps. Every sleep therefore ends at the sibling's end_walk, and both siblings can never be asleep at once.
- (d) So every held block is published in bounded time. The reader's next block (`taken`) is either still queued — and since the queue is FIFO, no worker holds any block then, so an idle worker takes it — or it is held, and finishes in bounded time. Slots free up and the scanner proceeds.
- Errors are published at the stage that finds them: MTF errors and BadOrigPtr at the front, CRC errors at the tail.
- Cancel: front_mtf drains the queue, walk_and_finish discards its result, and tables always go back to the pool.
- (e) The window does not bind: in the model, windows 8, 16 and 32 give −6.5%, −6.8% and −6.8% (outcome P, δ = 0.6), with idle-for-a-job time of 0.2-0.8% of worker time.

7. Fairness
- A sleeping sibling gets the token by direct handoff first; otherwise it goes to whoever reaches a stage end first.
- Within a worker, the oldest built block walks first.
- A worker can walk at most its two held blocks back to back before it must take new work. By then a waiting sibling is asleep and receives the handoff, so no worker waits more than 2 walks for the token.

8. Memory
- Tables: no extra 3.6 MB tables (2 per core = today's 4).
- ll: up to 2 per worker, +4 × 0.9 MB = +3.6 MB reserved.
- Returning symbols after MTF saves about 0.7 MB held on average.
- SegScratch: unchanged, one per worker.
- Net: about +2-4 MB on today's 80.1 MB peak RSS at 4t (OBSERVED, occupancy 42009406264).
- Live T-vectors (the tables the walk reads at random) in the model: mean 2.8 → 3.5-3.8; maximum 4 → 4.

9. Without SMT
- place() returns None when threads ≤ cores, when no core has 2 allowed CPUs (SMT off, cpusets, the bench's 2t run), and on non-Linux (allowed_cores is None). Then with_inverse::<Segmented> runs: today's decoder, bit for bit.
- Gap in the probe: if sched_setaffinity is refused, the pair keeps its token but may not share a core. The refinement is to disable a pair's token if either member fails to pin.
- The teams plan (6 or more cores) is untouched.

10. Variant for outcome M: the "memory token"
- The build also takes the token, so a walk and a build never run side by side on one core.
- Same code, plus a try_walk in step 2.
- Worth it only if the pair matrix shows the build is itself expensive beside a walk.

rivals.design:
CONSTRUCTION 3: one interleaved worker per physical core, instead of two SMT workers.

WHAT IT IS. On an SMT machine (CI: 4 vCPU = 2 cores) the plan runs one worker per physical core, pinned to CPUs 0 and 2; the sibling CPUs are left idle. Each worker carries two blocks:
- the W-slot holds block A in its walk, with its T-vector already built;
- the F-slot holds block B in its front phase.
The walk of A is interleaved, in one instruction stream, with the light latency-chain work of other blocks:
- MTF of B, the store-forward chain at src/mtf.rs:146-160;
- on worker 0, the stream's Huffman scanner (src/block.rs read_item), which is also a serial chain.
The build of B and the post-walk passes of A (RLE1, CRC) run uninterleaved, at the full core.

GRANULARITY: PER ROUND. The interleave point is the end of each j-iteration of the staged chunk loop (src/bwt.rs:1020-1147), where all 32 lanes have stepped once and the marked handoffs are done. A round is 32 lane-steps.
- OBSERVED (objdump of so2cg/sonly2 c30cg 0x3500f-0x3502c, whose block-1 Ir is 19,273,484 against 19,273,477 for d1fd4405): each step is 7 instructions plus 0.5 of loop overhead. The step is a load of rows[k], a load of t[row], test/js, a tile byte store, shr, a rows[k] store and a prefetcht0. That is 5 memory ops a step, so a round is about 240 instructions, or about 208 macro-ops.
- Against the retire queue (56665/57647/58455), a round fills 0.81 of Zen 3's 256 entries, 0.65 of Zen 4's 320 and 0.46 of Zen 5's 448. The window therefore holds about one round plus one filler slice, and the OoO engine can overlap them.
- Each lane's prefetch lead becomes the round plus the slice, so filler also lengthens the lead.
- Per tile is rejected: TILE 256 x 32 lanes is 8192 steps, about 61K instructions, far past any ROB. The two kernels would only alternate, which is the serial 2t.
- Per step is rejected: with 16 GPRs, MTF's roughly 10 live values would spill every switch, adding load and store ops to the pipes the walk already loads.

FILLER BUDGET (INFERRED). About 0.072 MTF moves per output byte (serial-stages) is about 2.3 moves, or about 3 MTF symbols, per 32-byte round. The budget is adaptive: k = ceil(remaining MTF moves / remaining walk rounds). It counts moves (the 20-24-cycle chain units), not symbols or instructions; this is AMAC's lesson, below. On worker 0 add about 2 Huffman lookups a round (0.0646 lookups/B). The chains per round are about 24 + 28 cycles, against the round's 61-138 cycles of walk issue.

STATE MACHINE, per worker.
- WalkTask is room_segments' existing explicit state hoisted out of the function: lanes[32], rows[32], tile[32][256], st[32], queued, done, w, j, room, and phase in {Fill, Full, Tail, Done}. round() runs one j-iteration.
- MtfCursor is mtf_avx2's loop with its state in a struct (list store, run, weight, n, syms index, counts) and step(moves). It follows the inner-loop-with-limit, outer-loop-for-the-cut pattern of mtf_checkpoints (mtf.rs:286-364), at about 1/250 of that grain.
- ScanCursor (worker 0 only) is a budgeted read_item.
- Loop:
  - while W is busy and a filler is pending: round(), then fill(k);
  - when MTF(B) and the scanner budget are exhausted, the walk runs alone;
  - when the walk ends, post(A) runs alone, then build(B) runs alone;
  - then B moves to W, and the next job enters F through the existing jobs channel (parallel.rs:418-426) and the ready map.
- Two T-vectors per core: today's 4t footprint (OBSERVED: 2 workers a core, live T-vectors mean 10.3 MB, occupancy 41976148952). RSS is about the same: half the workers, twice the scratch each.
- The scanner either folds into worker 0 or is time-sliced on CPUs 0 and 2. It never goes on a sibling, because under outcome C any busy sibling costs the walk about 2x.

WHY THESE PARTNERS (INFERRED from code and vendor tables).
- MTF and the scanner are L1-resident chain kernels with little issue, store or miss-buffer use. MTF is about 11 memory ops per move of about 30 instructions, about 1.1 memory ops per output byte, and about 0.3 stores per byte that stay in L1.
- The build is excluded. It scatters into 256 streams (bwt.rs:288-353), and its stores miss to L3.
  - x86-TSO commits stores in order through one 64-entry STQ on Zen 3/4. A missing build store at the head would block commit of the walk's 2 stores a step, the same coupling #171 removed from the walk itself (OBSERVED: -5% to -14% of 4t wall, walk-round.md:18-71).
  - SMT protects the walk from this, because the STQ is statically partitioned (56665 Table 3; 57647 Table 4). One stream cannot.
- Assembly, RLE1 and CRC are streaming passes and are excluded too. Assembly is the most co-run-inflated pass on AMD: x2.97 on the 7763 and x3.53 on the 9V74 (OBSERVED, phases 42011789918 and 42020095581).

ISSUE SLACK LEFT BY THE 32-LANE WALK.
- OBSERVED, alone: 10.45 Ir/B inclusive (callgrind so2cg/cg/sonly2-b1.out: room_segments 9,407,085 Ir for 899,971 B). At 4.33 / 4.22 / 2.89 / 7.27 c/B (7763 / 9V74 / 9V45 / 8370C) that is IPC 2.41 / 2.48 / 3.62 / 1.44, against dispatch 6 / 6 / 8 / 5.
- INFERRED: 59-71% of dispatch slots idle, which is 15.5 / 14.9 / 12.7 / 25.9 idle slots per byte. MTF+build+RLE1+CRC plus about 10% overhead needs about 11.8.
- LSU: 5 memory ops a step against 3 AGUs on Zen 3/4 gives a floor of 1.67 c/step, plus about 0.15 for flush, so about 1.8. That is the fitted lane-independent term a = 1.91 on the 9V74, and Zen 5's 5/4 = 1.25 floor is close to its a = 1.42 (walk.md FALSIFIER). So INFERRED: the walk's "issue" term is its LSU throughput. The other 51-55% of its alone time is the memory term lat/M = 52/22 = 2.36 c/B, which sits at the documented 24-entry MAB (walk.md:159-163).
- Lines in flight (Little's law, accounting FALSIFIER): 9.8 alone falling to 5.5 per thread at 4 copies (7763), 9.3 to 5.5 (9V74). Fitted knee M: 22 alone, 16 per thread at 4 copies (9V74). INFERRED, unproven: 16 is exactly the SMT STQ partition (32 entries / 2 stores a step), so the 4-copy knee may be the statically partitioned STQ.
- So the slack exists in count (about 55% of the walk's cycles). The warning is the fit's additivity: t = a + lat/M, meaning the walk's own independent lanes do not overlap their LSU work with the memory wait. Whatever blocks them during miss-buffer-full periods may also block filler memory ops. Only the microbenchmark below can tell.

DOES FILLER DISTURB THE WALK'S MLP (INFERRED).
- STQ use per round: walk 64 + MTF about 10. That leaves about 28 steps of window against 16 under SMT and 32 alone, so the miss-buffer cap of 22 stays binding: alone-level MLP is kept. With the build added (about 29 more stores, all missing), the window collapses as above.
- Miss buffers: MTF and the scanner take about 0. The build takes about 2-3 (0.094 new lines a row), and the streams about 2-4.
- MTF's store-forward stall holds retirement about 20 cycles, about 5 walk steps or 10 STQ entries: tolerable.
- MTF's data-dependent run/move mispredicts flush the younger walk round. SMT would not; this cost is in delta.
- L1D: the scanner's LUTs (up to 6 x 4 KiB) plus the 8 KiB tile plus prefetched lines are close to Zen 3/4's 32 KiB. No worse than today's scanner-on-sibling.

CAN 2 INTERLEAVED THREADS BEAT 4 SMT THREADS? They must achieve S_int at least the 2t to 4t gain over the serial one-thread-a-core decoder: 1.13-1.24 on the bench (OBSERVED), or 1.17-1.27 from the phases model.
- MTF alone as filler cannot do it. MTF is only 22-24% of serial per-core time, so hiding it fully gives S of 1.28-1.31 before coupling, about a tie.
- Folding the scanner in as a second chain filler is required. MTF plus scanner is about 3.2 c/B, 74% of the walk's time, so it fits inside the walk.
- On Intel the walk gains from SMT (yield 1.37 on the 8370C), which C3 forfeits.
- Verdict: C3 can beat 4t SMT only on AMD, only under outcome C, and only with an in-thread absorption e of at least 0.6-0.7 for MTF and scanner filler.

AMAC AND COOP: WHAT APPLIES.
- AMAC (Kocberber, Falsafi and Grot, PVLDB 9(4)) keeps per-lookup state in a circular buffer, with stage-independent progress and refill on completion. The room walk already is that, for homogeneous chains (mlp-scheduling.md:453; expert-review.md:165-178, E10 not run; compact-psi-feasibility.md:139-148, "AMAC adds nothing for uniform steps").
  - AMAC's lever is more independent misses, bounded by miss-status holding registers. That is exhausted: lanes 24-64 are flat at 4 copies (NOGO, sweeps 41989592674 and 41989596336).
  - C3 is AMAC generalised to heterogeneous tasks, filling issue/LSU slack at a fixed MLP. That AMAC does not study.
  - What transfers: explicit resumable state rather than stackful coroutines; sizing in-flight work to the miss-buffer pool; and AMAC's critique of fixed-stage software-pipelined prefetching. C3's filler slices have divergent costs (a move's 24-cycle chain against a run symbol's few cycles), so a fixed symbols-per-round budget is SPP-like. Budget in moves.
- Coop teams (Cooperative<K>, coop.rs) are the inverse decomposition: K cores per block, an L3-footprint lever, off below COOP_MIN_CORES = 6 (parallel.rs:494). On 2 cores teams halve the blocks in flight (nogo.md, closed).
  - The coop journal's open problem, helpers idle through MTF and CRC (phase-aware teams), is exactly the slack C3 spends: MTF becomes the walk's filler.
  - Nothing structural in coop is reusable on CI. mtf_checkpoints proves MTF can be sliced correctly.

rivals.gain_under_C:
Outcome C: any busy sibling, including the L1 ALU loop and the plain chain, costs the walk about 2x.
- INFERRED mechanism: SMT mode itself. On Zen 3/4 the STQ and retire queue are statically partitioned and the miss buffers and load queue are watermarked (56665 Table 3; 57647 Table 4). That would fit the 16-per-thread 4-copy knee being STQ/2.
- Pairing and walk tokens are then worth about 0 to -3%: a walk-exclusive core costs walk 4.33 + compute 4.68/1.43 against 7.85 a core today.
- C3 is the only construction that uses the walk's slack, because one stream runs with the unpartitioned structures. Light fillers (MTF, scanner) consume only about 10 of the 64 STQ entries a round.
- The matrix says nothing about in-thread absorption here, so the bounds stay wide.

4t wall versus master, AMD:

| variant | 7763 | 9V74 | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| C3+scanner (the design) | lo +12%, central -4%, hi -14% | lo +8%, central -8%, hi -18% | e >= 0.6-0.7 |
| C3-lite (MTF only) | lo +19%, central +7%, hi 0% | lo +15%, central +3%, hi -5% | not worth building |
| C3 with a staged build also interleaved | theoretical hi -31% | theoretical hi -34% | a staged build, which does not exist; unrealistic |

Intel (8370C), if C were seen there: C3+scan lo +18%, central +3.5%, hi -5%. The Intel walk gains from SMT (OBSERVED yield 1.37), so Intel is expected to be at or above 0. C3 would have to be gated to AMD.

Release caveat: C3 assumes idle siblings. Under C, any co-tenant on a sibling, such as wikidata-pq's other stages, costs the C3 walk about 2x again.
rivals.gain_under_M:
Outcome M: only memory-heavy siblings cost (walk, build, streaming read). The L1 ALU loop, the plain chain and MTF cost about 1.0-1.2x.
- The light fillers are then benign in hardware, so in-thread absorption is likely high, e about 0.85-0.95. The coupling delta of about 0.4 remains.
- C3+scanner, 4t wall versus master: 7763 central -8% (lo +3%, hi -14%); 9V74 central -12% (lo 0%, hi -18%). C3-lite: 7763 -0% to +7%; 9V74 -5% to +3%.
- But SMT pairing then reaches the same walk-side relief with no software overhead, independent retirement and no mispredict coupling. It also keeps SMT's 1.23-1.54x yield on build, post-walk and scanner, which C3 gives up by running the build and post-walk passes alone. Pairing estimate: about -15% to -20% of 4t wall (INFERRED: walk beside light work 1.0-1.2x, build beside build at the 7763's 1.43 yield).
- So C3 against pairing is 0% to +10% worse. C3 is dominated: close it, and route the effort to the pairing or token construction.
- Intel: C3+scan about 0% to +10% either way. Not pursued.
rivals.gain_under_P:
Outcome P: walk beside compute is materially cheaper than walk beside walk, for example 1.2-1.5x against 2.1-2.3x.
- In-thread light filler is again likely benign: e about 0.7-0.9, delta about 0.4.
- C3+scanner, 4t wall versus master: 7763 central -6% (lo +5%, hi -14%); 9V74 central -10% (lo +2%, hi -18%). C3-lite: about +7% to -5%.
- Pairing under P (serial-stages model: f_WC 1.2-1.5, f_NW 1.3-1.4) gives about -17% to -25% of core time. C3 matches it only at e at least about 0.9 with delta at most about 0.2.
- C3 is dominated, unless pairing's realised gain is lost to OS phase alignment (a scheduler cannot always find a compute block beside each walk). The residual case for C3 under P is determinism: in-thread pairing never misses its partner.
- Judgement: close C3, or keep it only as a fallback if a pairing PR measures under half its modelled gain.
rivals.needs_from_pair_matrix:
Requested from the pair matrix, on at least 2 AMD models (Zen 3 7763, plus a Zen 4/5) and one Intel model. Fastest-of-5 and median figures should both be reported, because the fastest bias alone moves the factors 0.1-0.15 (walk.md unknown 7).

1. THE GATE. The walk on CPU 0 beside an L1 ALU loop and beside the plain chain on CPU 1, against idle.
   - Both at least about 1.6x: outcome C, and C3 stays live.
   - Both at most about 1.25x: outcome M or P. C3 closes in favour of pairing.
2. MECHANISM WITHIN C. The plain-chain factor, about 1 line in flight and few ops, against walk beside walk.
   - About equal (about 2x): static partitioning (STQ/ROB). C3 helps only with store-light fillers, which the design already restricts to.
   - Clearly smaller (about 1.3-1.4x): the miss-buffer and load-queue watermark. C3 regains the full 24-entry pool, so it is the more favourable case.
   - If possible, also an "active but idle" sibling (a pause or divide loop), to separate partitioning from arbitration.
3. THE COMPETITOR'S PRICE. Walk beside MTF and walk beside the scanner, plus MTF and scanner beside the walk. These price SMT pairing; under M/P they also bound C3's in-thread cost from below.
4. EXCLUSIONS. Walk beside build and beside a streaming read, expected about 2x under M. They confirm that the build and post-walk passes must stay out of the filler.
5. CROSS-CORE. The walk on CPUs {0,2} against alone. This is amp2, applied to C3's two busy cores; the model uses 1.04-1.11. Above 1.12 would push C3's break-even e up by about 0.1.
6. INTEL ROWS. If the 8370C walk beside a walk keeps an SMT yield above 1.2, C3 is confirmed off on Intel, and any plan must be vendor-gated.
rivals.minimal_prototype:
STAGE 1: A FILLER MICROBENCHMARK. It measures e directly, without building the decoder, and goes in the full tier only: sweep.yml dispatch, about 5-6 min, nothing added to the PR tier.

What to build:
- A const-generic per-round hook on room_segments (H: RoundHook, default NoHook). It is called after each j-iteration (bwt.rs:1147).
- Identity check, as #183's coresident branch did: the default instantiation must keep the same Ir (19,273,477 on wikidata block 1) and an identical objdump of room_segments::<32,1>.
- A new `fill` tool in examples/sweep.rs. Single thread on CPU 1, sibling idle, block pairs (A, B = next), timing:
  - (a) walk(A) alone;
  - (b) each filler alone;
  - (c) walk(A) with the filler inside it, k per round.
- Fillers:
  - MtfCursor over B, k = 1, 2, 4, 8 moves per round. It is mtf_avx2's loop with explicit state and step(moves), modelled on mtf_checkpoints' outer loop. Test: random budgets must give identical ll and counts to mtf().
  - ALU-only control: 4 independent xorshift chains, 8-64 ops per round. This measures pure dispatch slack.
  - L1 read-modify-write control: k increments on a 1 KiB array. This measures LSU slack.
  - ScanCursor, a budgeted read_item, k = 1, 2, 4 lookups. Stage 1b only, if 1a's MTF passes.
- Report e(k) = (T_walk + T_fill - T_both) / T_fill per filler, k and CPU model.
- Dispatch until a Zen 3, a Zen 4/5 and an Intel model have each been covered (runner assignment is random).

Decision rule, registered before running. Proceed to stage 2 only if all of these hold:
- the pair matrix shows outcome C on AMD;
- e_MTF >= 0.7 and e_scan >= 0.6 at the best k, on 2 AMD models;
- the cost model then projects at least -5% of 4t wall for C3+scan.
Otherwise C3 closes: a journal entry in docs/journal, and a line in the queue's Rejected list.
The controls also tell us something on their own. A high ALU e with a low L1-RMW e would confirm that the miss-buffer-full LSU blocking implied by the fit's additivity is real, which predicts the rule fails.
Cost: about 150-250 lines (hook, MtfCursor, tool rows, equivalence test). Miri risk is low: the hook does not touch walk state.

STAGE 2: THE DECODER PROTOTYPE, only if stage 1 passes.
- Plan::Interleaved in src/parallel.rs, AMD with SMT only.
- One pinned worker per physical core. Pinning needs sched_setaffinity through an extern declaration, since std has no affinity call.
- The W/F slot state machine. WalkTask hoists room_segments' state, so Miri and the segment oracle must cover a yield at every j.
- MTF of the F block as filler on both workers; the scanner folded into worker 0; build and post-walk passes alone.
- A bench A/B at 4t, with a parity check and memory parity.
rivals.risks:
1. ADDITIVITY (most likely to kill C3). The fitted walk is a + lat/M: its own independent lanes do not overlap LSU work with the memory wait. If miss-buffer saturation stalls the load/store pipes, filler memory ops are blocked too, and only ALU filler absorbs. Stage 1's L1-RMW control against the ALU control tests exactly this.
2. ONE RETIREMENT POINT. A walk demand miss blocks the filler's retirement, and MTF's roughly 20-24-cycle store-forward wait blocks the walk's. SMT retires each thread independently.
3. MISPREDICT COUPLING. MTF's run/move branches flush the younger walk round. The estimate is 0.1-0.5 c/B, which is most of delta. Mitigations: branchless MTF (owned by the MTF workflow) or placing the slice at the end of the round.
4. x86-TSO IN-ORDER STORE COMMIT IN ONE STQ. Any store-missing filler (the build's 256 streams, assembly, RLE1 output) recreates the pre-#171 store-stream stall for the walk. This is why the design excludes them, and why C3-max needs a staged build first.
5. THE GAIN IS SMALL AGAINST THE BAR. MTF-only filler at best ties with today's 4t (-0.1% / -4.7%). The win needs the scanner folded into a worker, which couples supply to worker 0's progress and makes the scanner resumable.
6. C3 FORFEITS SMT'S YIELD on everything not interleaved: the build at x1.43-2.25 and the post-walk passes. Under outcomes M/P this makes C3 strictly worse than pairing.
7. INTEL. The walk gains from SMT (yield 1.37 on the 8370C; no data on the 8573C, whose 2t to 4t gain of 1.244 is the highest), so C3 is expected at or above 0 there. It needs a vendor/model gate, which is fragile. The master bench lands on random models.
8. L1D PRESSURE. The scanner's LUTs (up to 24 KiB) plus the 8 KiB tile plus prefetched lines against 32 KiB on Zen 3/4.
9. IMBALANCE. The walk takes 4.33 c/B against MTF 1.98: only 46% of the walk can carry MTF, and with the scanner about 74%. Block-size variance, the stream's head and tail, and short blocks (below 64Ki rows they are walked plainly) all run unpaired.
10. RELEASE SHAPE. C3 assumes idle siblings. In wikidata-pq's split, co-tenants on the siblings bring back the SMT cost under outcome C.
11. COMPLEXITY AND SAFETY. Hoisting room_segments' unsafe state (tile, room, flush and handoff invariants, bwt.rs:852-866) into a resumable task needs Miri and the segment oracle at every yield point, plus a resumable MTF. Pinning needs an affinity syscall beyond what std offers.
12. MEASUREMENT BIAS. The phases 4-copy figures are fastest of 5. The model's 2t to 4t gain (1.17-1.27) is above the bench's 1.13-1.24, which shifts every C3 figure by 0-7 points, in C3's favour.

collision.failures:
Where each cost model fails. Tags: OBSERVED means pinned to a run id or file:line; INFERRED means the derivation is shown. The throwaway probes are in collide/ (probe_today.py, probe_repair.py, probe_des.py). They import the designs' own sim.py and des.py unchanged.

C1, STAGE-SPECIALISED PAIRS
1. Pinning each thread to one CPU breaks work conservation, which the model prices at ±1%. [INFERRED]
- The walker and the compute thread are each pinned to a single CPU, and only the walker may walk.
- The scanner (9.7-10.7% of 4t CPU), the reader (~3%) and the bench sampler (on the decoder CPUs at 4t, bench/CHANGELOG.md:150-170) float.
- Today each block is preempted 0.82-0.99 times and waits 0.27-0.35 ms in the run queue, 12.5-13.4% of decode elapsed (OBSERVED, serial-stages MISSED 4). Migration absorbs this today.
- In C1's own balance, AMD is walker-bound (by 11% on the 7763, 19% on the 9V74). There, a floater's slice on a walker CPU is lost walk throughput: the walker cannot move to its sibling, and the compute thread may not walk.
- Bound: 0 to +3% of 4t wall.
- Its prototype arm "scanner restricted to the walker CPUs" sits on the wrong side for a walker-bound core. C2's pinning to the core's 2-CPU mask avoids the problem.
2. The model, the gate and the design use three different thread layouts. [OBSERVED: stagespec/sim.py run_staged, and the design text]
- The sim folds the scanner into the compute chain (stage "SM").
- Step A's compute thread "runs the scanner as part of its jobs".
- The shipped design keeps the scanner as its own unpinned thread.
- So step A does not gate what would ship.
3. Its M gain is the strongest M on offer, not the middle of the range. [INFERRED, probe_today.py and probe_repair.py]
- Under its M pattern, its pinned 'today' sim locks the two threads' walks together. The walk's sibling is walking for 0.90 / 0.91 / 0.84 of walk time (7763 / 9V74 / 8370C), against 0.54 / 0.56 / 0.51 under C.
- That lock is what lets f(W|light) = 1.12 reproduce the mixed 2.12.
- The gain survives re-drawing partners at every block end: staged against a re-paired today gives -16.6 / -18.2 / -8.2% core time (against -18.4 / -19.4 / -9.6% against the pinned today). The re-paired today still locks, at 0.83 / 0.86 / 0.74.
- C2's calibration of M gives f(W|light) 1.42-1.78, so C1's -16% central is the top of the M range.
4. Its cap "f(W|W) <= 2.2 caps the AMD walk term at about 2%" is not identified. [INFERRED] The cap needs F_W = p f(W|W) + (1-p) f(W|N) with p = s_W, which assumes random phase. If the walks lock (under M or P), the observed mixed factor is mostly f(W|W). Only a measured f(W|N) can bound the walk term.
5. Segment assembly stays on the walker, beside compute work, folded into W. It is the most co-run-inflated AMD pass: x2.97 on the 7763 and x3.53 on the 9V74 (OBSERVED, phases 42011789918 and 42020095581).
6. Scope. [OBSERVED: parallel.rs:540-555; wikidata-pq dump.py BZ2_THREADS_CAP, one thread a physical core] It engages only at threads == 2 x cores below 6 cores: the CI 4t row. The release ETA does not change.

C2, WALK TOKEN
1. Its calibration under M and P. [OBSERVED des.py:24-57; INFERRED probe_des.py]
- calib() fixes p_W = 0.526 in an arithmetic mixture.
- Its own DES 'today' arm partially locks under M. Walk-beside-walk is 0.62 / 0.65 of walk time at δ_M 0.6 and 0.70 / 0.70 at δ_M 1.0 (7763 / 9V74), against 0.54 / 0.56 under C. Its totals stay within +0.4% to +1.0% of observed.
- So its M is the mild one, and its -3.5% M central is the bottom of the range.
- At matched δ_M = 1.0 its walk token gives -9.7% / -9.3% core time, against C1's -16.6 / -18.2. The rest of the -16% vs -3.5% gap is calibration. The design difference is about 7 points: C1's walker never meets a walk, and meets a build only about 37% of the time.
2. Its idle credit assumes a parked vCPU halts at once. The model gives 1-11% of walk time beside an idle sibling at alone speed, plus the parked sibling. In a guest, the idle governor can pick a polling state for short predicted idles, and a polling sibling is a busy sibling to the core. This is unmeasured on CI.
3. Under C it loses on Intel (+3% central, +8.5% worst, its own figures). Yet place() engages on any SMT-2 topology with threads > cores. It needs per-model gating, and only a measured Intel row can set it.
4. Untested.
- The code has not been compiled (OBSERVED, its own status).
- Its try_lock + try_recv path reads WouldBlock as "no job". At 4t today, workers already sit idle 1.7-2.4% of their time with a job queued (OBSERVED, serial-stages MISSED 3), so this path matters.
5. It has no cache term for a built table that waits for the token. The sibling's walk evicts the build's L2 residue (0.5-1.25 MB of a 3.6 MB table). walk.md FALSIFIER prices an L2 hit-rate change of 0.14 -> 0.26 at 1.5-2% of wall, so this loss is at most about 0.5-1% [INFERRED].
6. Scope: as C1.

C3, INTERLEAVE
1. The filler does not fit where C3 says the slack is. [INFERRED, from C3's own numbers]
- C3 itself infers that the walk's a-term is LSU throughput: 5 memory ops a step against 3 AGUs, a floor of 1.67 c/step, fitted a = 1.91 on the 9V74.
- So during the a-phase, the filler's memory ops (MTF about 1.1 per byte) add LSU work, about +0.37 c/B on Zen 3/4. They are not hidden.
- During the stall phase (lat/M, 51-55% of the alone time), the ROB is the window. A round is about 208 macro-ops (C3's objdump), which leaves 48 entries on Zen 3 (ROB 256), 112 on Zen 4 (320) and 240 on Zen 5 (448).
- The MTF filler is about 95-105 instructions a round (3.31 Ir/B x 32 B, callgrind sonly2-b1), and the scanner adds about 40-50.
- So on the 7763 the absorption e is about 0.35-0.55, against C3's break-even of 0.63-0.69. Zen 4 is marginal (e about 0.5-0.7 against 0.53-0.59).
- Corrected central under C: the 7763 about +4% to +15% (slower), the 9V74 about -6% to +6%.
2. The scanner is one serial chain for both cores' blocks. [INFERRED]
- Folded into worker 0, it needs about 4 lookups a round, not 2.
- Handed between workers at block ends, it advances only while its host is walking (about 55-60% of the time), so supply can fall behind consumption.
- C3 prices it as (1-e_s) scan / 2 per core, as if it were split across both walks.
3. Keeping the siblings idle is not the library's choice. [OBSERVED: the bench's main thread takes 0.02-0.04 s CPU per 4t run (serial-stages MACHINE); the sampler sits on the siblings at 2t (CHANGELOG.md:166-168); wikidata-pq's parse workers share the cores (dump.py)]
- The library cannot pin the caller's reader thread, and the scheduler puts it on an idle sibling, beside a walk.
- Under C this costs +1% to +3% of 4t wall in the bench [INFERRED: about 4.5% of each sibling's time x walk share 0.55 x 1.12].
- In a release, the siblings belong to wikidata-pq's other stages.
4. MTF(B) runs a whole walk before build(B), so ll (0.9 MB) leaves L2, and the build reads it twice from L3: about +0.1-0.3 c/B [INFERRED].
5. It gives up the SMT yield on the build and the post-walk passes (the build's yield is 1.43 on the 7763), so under M and P it is dominated, by its own analysis.
6. Engaged at 4t, C3 runs the 2t layout, so the 2t bench row measures it directly. The model never uses this.
collision.shared_assumptions:
1. THE WALK'S OWN FOOTPRINT IS A CONSTANT (all three). This is the assumption whose failure kills all three as first choices.
- C1 and C2 make the walk's co-run cost a function of the sibling's stage, f(W|Y). C3 makes it a function of whether the sibling runs at all. None lets the walk's own per-step claim on the core's partitioned structures vary.
- Yet the largest 4t lever measured was exactly that kind of change. #171 staged the walk's stores: 4t CPU -17.6% / -16.3% with 1t flat on the 9V45. Its journal reads the mechanism as "mostly lower contention between SMT siblings" (OBSERVED: docs/journal/2026-11-05-staged-walk.md result table; runs 41952512753, 41956321455).
- The 4-copy factor follows each kernel's own per-byte work: on the 7763, plain (one chain) x1.18, bitmap x2.16, flagged x2.13, room x2.12 (OBSERVED, phases 42011789918).
